cohort_sampling_contract.disjointness: each later R1 cohort excludes all earlier R1 cohort task files in addition to every prior Pilot 0 task set, so no prestate may appear in more than one R1 cohort
cohort_sampling_contract.interpretation: same manipulation, assay, model, generation contract, and prestate-sampling distribution; different sampled prestates

primary_endpoint.name: T_instability
primary_endpoint.definition: within one encoding arm's two E0 branches, 1 iff their final answers differ, else 0
primary_endpoint.cohort_estimand: Delta_c = mean_i D_i within cohort c
primary_endpoint.common_estimand: Delta_common = arithmetic mean of the four prespecified cohort effects Delta_1...Delta_4; cohorts receive equal weight as independent replication draws

randomization_inference.rule: within every prestate block, shuffle the four branch outcomes and reassign exact 2/2 fields/prose labels; recompute each cohort Delta_c and the equal-cohort Delta_common

decision.reason: Delta_common differs from zero under the prespecified blocked-randomization test.

transport_diagnostic.interpretation: Cochran Q p>=0.05 indicates compatibility with a common-effect model under this diagnostic; it does not establish transport invariance.

analysis_contract.cohort_reporting: report Delta_c and a 95% whole-block bootstrap interval for every cohort before pooled inference
analysis_contract.common_effect_interval: stratified whole-block bootstrap: independently resample blocks with replacement within each cohort, recompute Delta_c, then average the four cohort effects equally
analysis_contract.common_effect_test: two-sided blocked randomization test for Delta_common=0 under the sharp no-encoding-effect null: within every prestate block, shuffle RF_E0/RP_E0 labels preserving exact 2/2, recompute each cohort Delta_c and their equal-cohort mean
analysis_contract.common_effect_practical_scale: practical equivalence requires the 95% stratified-bootstrap interval for Delta_common to lie strictly inside [-0.05,+0.05]
transport_assessment_order: between-cohort dispersion relative to estimated sampling uncertainty
analysis_contract.transport_model: Cochran Q common-effect compatibility diagnostic using cohort-specific sampling variances Var(D_i)/n_c; report Q, df=3, chi-square p-value, I^2, and DerSimonian-Laird tau^2 descriptively
analysis_contract.transport_guard: if any cohort has zero/nonfinite estimated sampling variance, mark Q/I2/tau2 not adjudicable rather than regularizing silently
analysis_contract.transport_interpretation: Q p>=0.05 means observed cohort effects are compatible with a common-effect model under this diagnostic; it does not establish transport invariance. Q p<0.05 is evidence of excess between-cohort dispersion and earns a transport/heterogeneity follow-up.

interpretation_guardrails: R1 is a replication/transport branch, not continuation of the A-series localization ladder.
T_instability is the sole primary endpoint because R1 prospectively targets the A5-A7 replication discrepancy.
Different cohort point estimates do not by themselves establish heterogeneity.
Failure to detect between-cohort variation does not establish perfect transport invariance.
A significant common effect does not imply a practically large effect; causal/nonzero and practical-scale claims remain separate.
A transport signal does not identify why cohorts differ; prestate composition, sampling variation beyond model assumptions, or other context dependence require later discrimination.
No R1 result automatically updates B, C, H1, I1, S, or CARS.
